scenarios.title: Implementation plan for invoice export
scenarios.prompt:
The requirements and design for the invoice export feature are approved and sit in docs/specs/invoice-export/ in our repo. I need the implementation plan for our coding agent to work through, and I'll commit it next to them. Both documents are below.

Requirements

1. Requesting an export
1.1 A finance user can request a CSV export of invoices for a date range of up to 12 months.
1.2 The export runs in the background. When it is ready the user gets an email with a download link.
1.3 Download links expire after 24 hours.

2. Contents
2.1 Each row has invoice number, customer, issue date, currency, net, tax and total.
2.2 Amounts are written in the invoice's own currency with two decimals.
2.3 A range with no invoices produces a file with only the header row.

3. Access
3.1 Only users with the finance role can request or download an export.
3.2 A caller without the role gets a 403 and nothing is created.
3.3 A download link works only for the user who requested the export.

4. Failures
4.1 If rendering fails, the job is marked failed, the user gets an email saying so, and no partial file is left in storage.
4.2 A range longer than 12 months is rejected with a message that names the limit.
4.3 If an email cannot be sent it is retried up to 3 times, and the failure is logged.

5. Audit
5.1 Every request and every download is written to the audit log with the user, the range and the time.

Design
- ExportRequest: DynamoDB item with id, userId, range, status, fileKey and expiresAt.
- ExportRepository: create, get, markReady, markFailed.
- InvoiceSource: reads invoices from the billing API in pages of 500.
- CsvWriter: streams rows to S3 as a multipart upload and aborts the upload on error.
- ExportService: validates the range, creates the request and queues the job. The worker uses InvoiceSource and CsvWriter, then marks the request ready.
- Notifier: sends the ready and failed emails with retry.
- API: POST /exports and GET /exports/{id}/download, behind the existing auth middleware.
- AuditLogger: the shared logger the API handlers call for audit records.
- Tests with Jest.
rubric: A task covers the empty range: an export with no invoices in the range produces a file with only the header row (2.3).
A task covers retrying a failed email up to 3 times and logging the failure (4.3).
Every task names the numbered requirements it serves, including the tasks for the repository and the audit logger, which the requirements do not name.
The worker, the CSV writer and the notifier each get their own task or sub-task; no single task covers more than one of them.
Says the plan is saved in docs/specs/invoice-export/ with the requirements and design, and names no other location for it.
Tasks build on earlier ones: the repository, invoice source and CSV writer come before the service that uses them, and the service comes before the API handlers.
Each task says what to create or change by name, such as the classes, functions or files from the design, and not only a goal.
Tasks are numbered and each has a box that can be ticked off.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: A twelve-point requirements list in which several items are error or edge cases (empty range, email retry, link ownership), and a design with components the requirements never name (repository, audit logger). The folder for the spec files is given. The plan has to link tasks to requirements (r01), cover the edge cases (r06), keep the worker, writer and notifier apart (r07) and be filed with the spec (r12).

scenarios.title: Implementation plan for team invitations
scenarios.prompt:
Here are the approved requirements and design for team invitations. Please turn them into the implementation plan for our coding agent.

Requirements

1. Sending
1.1 A workspace admin can invite someone by email address.
1.2 A member who is not an admin cannot send invitations.
1.3 An address that already belongs to a member is rejected with a message saying so.
1.4 The invitation email contains a link that is valid for 7 days.
1.5 Members plus open invitations cannot exceed the plan's seat limit. A request over the limit is refused and says how many seats are left.

2. Managing
2.1 An admin sees open invitations with the email, the sender and the expiry date.
2.2 An admin can revoke an open invitation. A revoked link stops working at once.
2.3 An admin can resend an invitation at most 3 times a day. Sending a new email makes the earlier link stop working.

3. Accepting
3.1 A valid link shows the workspace name and lets the person join with an existing account or create one.
3.2 An expired or revoked link shows a clear message and a way to ask the admin for a new invitation.
3.3 If the person is already a member, the link just opens the workspace.
3.4 Accepting takes one seat and removes the open invitation.

4. Records
4.1 Sending, revoking, resending and accepting are written to the audit log.

Design
- Invitation: DynamoDB item with id, workspaceId, email, tokenHash, status, expiresAt, resendCount and resendDay.
- TokenService: creates a random token; only its hash is stored.
- InvitationRepository: create, findByTokenHash, listOpen, update.
- SeatService: counts members plus open invitations against the plan limit.
- InvitationService: send, revoke, resend and accept. It uses the token service, the repository, the seat service and the Mailer.
- Mailer: wraps the existing email client.
- API: POST, GET and DELETE under /workspaces/{id}/invitations and POST /invitations/accept, behind the existing admin guard where an admin is required.
- Accept page in the existing React app.
- Jest tests for the backend and React Testing Library for the page.
rubric: A task covers refusing a send from a member who is not an admin (1.2).
A task covers limiting resends to 3 a day and making the earlier link stop working (2.3).
Every task names the numbered requirements it serves, including the tasks for the token service and the seat service, which the requirements do not name.
Sending, revoking, resending and accepting are built in separate tasks or sub-tasks, not in one step that implements the whole invitation service.
Tasks build on earlier ones: the token service, repository and seat service come before the invitation service, and that service comes before the API endpoints and the accept page.
Each task says what to create or change by name, such as the classes, endpoints or files from the design, and not only a goal.
The plan has at most two levels: top-level tasks with sub-tasks directly beneath them, and nothing nested deeper.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: Fifteen numbered criteria with a mix of happy path, permission and limit rules, and a service in the design that does four different things. The plan has to keep every rule (r06), say which criteria each task serves, including the helper services that no criterion names (r01), and not collapse the four operations into one step (r07).

scenarios.title: Implementation plan for API keys and rate limits
scenarios.prompt:
Please write the implementation plan for the API key and rate limit feature from the approved documents below. The coding agent starts on it tomorrow.

Requirements

1. Keys
1.1 A developer can create up to 5 API keys per project. A sixth is refused with a message naming the limit.
1.2 The secret is shown once, when the key is created, and never again.
1.3 A project owner can rotate a key. The old secret keeps working for 24 hours after rotation.
1.4 A project owner can revoke a key. It stops working within a minute.

2. Limits
2.1 Each key allows 600 requests per minute by default.
2.2 A project owner can change a key's limit, up to the plan maximum.
2.3 A request over the limit gets a 429 response with a Retry-After header.
2.4 When a key is revoked its limit counters are removed.

3. Access
3.1 Only project owners can create, rotate, revoke or change the limit of a key. Developers can list keys.
3.2 The key list shows name, last four characters, created date, last used date and status, and never the secret.

4. Usage
4.1 Requests per key per day are recorded.
4.2 The usage page shows the last 30 days, including the number of 429 responses per day.
4.3 Usage records older than 90 days are deleted.

5. Alerts
5.1 The owner is emailed when a key stays above 80% of its limit for 5 minutes in a row, at most once a day per key.
5.2 The owner is emailed when a key is rotated or revoked by someone else.

Design
- ApiKey: DynamoDB item with id, projectId, name, secretHash, last4, status, limitPerMin, graceUntil and lastUsedAt.
- KeyStore: create, find by secret hash, list, update.
- KeyService: create with the 5-key check, rotate with the grace period, revoke, change limit. The owner checks happen here.
- RateLimiter: token bucket in Redis keyed by key id; returns allowed or a retry-after value.
- Gateway middleware: authenticates the key (including a rotated one during its grace period), applies the limiter, records usage and returns the 429.
- UsageRecorder: increments the daily counters and runs a scheduled cleanup.
- AlertJob: runs every minute, checks the 80% condition and sends the emails through the existing Mailer.
- Console pages: key list with create and rotate dialogs, and the usage page.
- Jest tests; Redis through the existing client.
rubric: A task covers deleting usage records older than 90 days (4.3).
A task covers emailing the owner when a key is rotated or revoked by someone else (5.2).
A task covers removing a key's limit counters when it is revoked (2.4).
Every task names the numbered requirements it serves, and the tasks for the gateway middleware and the usage recorder, which no requirement names, say which requirements they support.
The rate limiter, the gateway middleware and the usage recorder are separate tasks or sub-tasks, not one step that builds the gateway.
Tasks build on earlier ones: the key store and key service come before the middleware that authenticates keys, and the limiter comes before the middleware that applies it.
Each task says what to create or change by name, such as the classes, endpoints or files from the design, and not only a goal.
Sub-tasks are shown nested beneath the parent task they belong to, not as a flat list.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: Seventeen criteria, three of them small clean-up or notification items that sit at the end of their groups (usage deletion after 90 days, counters removed on revoke, an email when someone else rotates a key), and two design components (gateway middleware, usage recorder) that no criterion names. A plan built around the main flow drops the small items silently (r06) or leaves the design-only parts without a requirement link (r01).

scenarios.title: Implementation plan for document upload with scanning
scenarios.prompt:
The approved spec for document upload is below; the files live in design/doc-upload/. Please write the implementation plan the coding agent will follow.

Requirements

1. Upload
1.1 A signed-in user can upload a PDF, PNG or JPEG of up to 25 MB to a case.
1.2 Other types or larger files are rejected before the upload starts, with a message that names the allowed types and the size limit.
1.3 The upload goes straight to storage through a signed URL that lasts 5 minutes. Only users with edit rights on the case can get one.

2. Scanning
2.1 Every upload is scanned for malware before anyone can download it.
2.2 Until the scan finishes the document shows as scanning and cannot be downloaded.
2.3 An infected file is deleted, the uploader is told, and the case timeline records it.
2.4 If the scanner is unavailable the document stays in scanning and the scan is retried for up to 1 hour. After that it is marked scan failed and a message goes to the on-call channel.

3. Download
3.1 Users with view rights on the case can download clean documents.
3.2 Download links expire after 5 minutes.

4. Housekeeping
4.1 Uploads that never complete are removed after 24 hours.
4.2 Documents on a closed case are deleted 7 years after it closes.

Design
- Document: DynamoDB item with id, caseId, name, size, type, status, uploadedBy and createdAt.
- CaseAccess: existing module; add canEdit and canView helpers.
- UploadService: validates type and size, checks edit rights, creates the Document as uploading and returns the signed URL.
- Storage: one bucket with a quarantine prefix for new uploads.
- ScanWorker: Lambda on the upload event. It calls the scanner, moves clean files out of quarantine and updates the status.
- ScanRetry: SQS delay queue for scans that could not start; after an hour it sets scan failed and posts to the on-call channel.
- DownloadService: checks view rights and status, then returns a signed URL.
- CleanupJob: scheduled Lambda for incomplete uploads and expired retention.
- Upload widget in the case page showing the status of each document.
rubric: A task covers an unavailable scanner: the scan is retried for up to an hour, then the document is marked scan failed and on-call is told (2.4).
A task covers removing uploads that never complete after 24 hours (4.1).
Says the plan is saved in design/doc-upload/ with the requirements and design, and names no other location for it.
Every task names the numbered requirements it serves.
The scan worker, the retry path and the cleanup job are separate tasks or sub-tasks, not one step that implements scanning and housekeeping.
Tasks build on earlier ones: the access helpers and the document model come before the upload and download services, and the scan worker comes before the retry path that feeds on it.
Requirement references appear in the same place and the same form in every task, for example always on the last line of the task.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: A scanning pipeline with an outage path (retry for an hour, then a failed state and an alert) and a housekeeping job, both described at the tail of their groups. The folder is named only as where the files live. The plan has to carry the outage path and the cleanup (r06), keep scanning, retry and cleanup apart (r07), link tasks to criteria (r01) and be filed in the named folder (r12).

scenarios.title: Implementation plan for order cancellation and refunds
scenarios.prompt:
The requirements and design for order cancellation and refunds are approved and pasted below. I need the plan for our coding agent.

Requirements

1. Cancelling
1.1 A customer can cancel an order that has not shipped, from the order page.
1.2 If an order is partly shipped, cancelling cancels only the lines that have not shipped.
1.3 A fully shipped order cannot be cancelled. The page does not offer it, and the API refuses with a 409.

2. Refunds
2.1 Cancelling a paid order refunds the cancelled lines, including their share of tax and shipping.
2.2 Refunds go back to the original payment method.
2.3 If the payment provider rejects a refund, the order shows refund pending. The refund is retried every hour for 3 days, then support is alerted.
2.4 The same line is never refunded twice, even if the cancel request is repeated.

3. Support
3.1 A support agent can cancel on a customer's behalf and must give a reason. Agents can see the refund status.
3.2 Only agents with the orders:cancel permission can do this.

4. Follow-up
4.1 The customer gets an email confirming the cancellation and the refund amount.
4.2 Stock for cancelled lines goes back to inventory.
4.3 The order history shows who cancelled, when and why.

Design
- Order and OrderLine: existing models; an OrderLine status is open, shipped or cancelled.
- RefundRecord: new item with id, orderId, lineIds, amount, status, attempts and idempotencyKey.
- CancellationPolicy: pure function that decides which lines can be cancelled.
- RefundCalculator: works out each line's share of tax and shipping.
- PaymentAdapter: wraps the provider's refund call and passes the idempotency key.
- RefundService: creates the record, calls the adapter and updates the status.
- RefundRetryJob: hourly job for pending refunds.
- InventoryClient: restocks lines.
- CancellationService: runs the policy, then the refund, inventory, email and history steps.
- API: customer endpoint and agent endpoint with the permission check.
- Mailer: existing email client.
rubric: A task covers never refunding the same line twice when the cancel request is repeated (2.4).
A task covers retrying a rejected refund every hour for 3 days and alerting support after that (2.3).
A task covers letting only agents with the orders:cancel permission cancel on a customer's behalf (3.2).
Every task names the numbered requirements it serves.
The refund calculation, the payment adapter and the retry job are separate tasks or sub-tasks, not one step that builds refunds.
Tasks build on earlier ones: the policy, calculator and payment adapter come before the refund service, and that service comes before the cancellation service and the endpoints.
Each task says what to create or change by name, such as the classes, functions or endpoints from the design, and not only a goal.
Tasks are numbered and each has a box that can be ticked off.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: A cancellation flow whose hard parts are rules that never show on the happy path: no double refund on a repeated request, the hourly retry window with an alert, and the permission for agents. The design has many collaborating services, so order matters and one step per area is tempting. Tests that each rule gets a task (r06), tasks name their criteria (r01) and refund pieces stay separate (r07).

scenarios.title: Implementation plan for notification preferences in a monorepo package
scenarios.prompt:
The requirements and design for notification preferences are approved; they are in packages/notifications/specs/preferences/. Please write the implementation plan for our coding agent.

Requirements

1. Channels and categories
1.1 A user can turn each category (billing, security, product news) on or off for each channel (email, push, SMS).
1.2 Security notifications cannot be turned off for email. The toggle is shown disabled with an explanation.
1.3 New users start with every category on for email and push, and SMS off.

2. Quiet hours
2.1 A user can set quiet hours with a start, an end and a time zone. Push and SMS that would be sent in that window are held and delivered when it ends.
2.2 Security notifications ignore quiet hours.
2.3 Changing the time zone applies to future notifications only.

3. Digest
3.1 Product news can be immediate or a daily digest at 09:00 in the user's time zone.

4. Applying preferences
4.1 Every send checks the user's preferences first.
4.2 If the preferences store cannot be reached, security notifications are sent anyway and all others are held and retried for up to 15 minutes.
4.3 A change takes effect within a minute.

5. Access and history
5.1 A user can read and change only their own preferences. Admins can read them but not change them.
5.2 Every change records who changed what and when.

Design
- Preferences: DynamoDB item per user with the channel matrix, quiet hours, digest mode, time zone and a version.
- PreferenceStore: get and put with the version check, and a 30 second cache.
- PreferenceService: validates changes (including the security rule), writes them and records the history entry.
- PreferenceGate: library the senders call with the user, category, channel and time. It answers send, hold until a time, or drop, and it holds the outage fallback.
- HoldQueue: SQS delay queue for held messages.
- DigestJob: hourly scheduler that sends the digests for users whose local time is 09:00.
- API: GET and PUT /me/preferences, and GET /users/{id}/preferences for admins.
- Settings page in the React app.
- History table written by the preference service.
rubric: Says the plan is saved in packages/notifications/specs/preferences/ with the requirements and design, and names no other location for it.
A task covers the outage rule: when the preferences store cannot be reached, security notifications still go out and the rest wait up to 15 minutes for retry (4.2).
A task covers refusing a change that turns off security email, with the toggle shown disabled and an explanation (1.2).
Every task names the numbered requirements it serves.
The gate, the hold queue and the digest job are separate tasks or sub-tasks, not one step that applies preferences.
Tasks build on earlier ones: the store comes before the service and the gate, and the service comes before the API and the settings page.
The plan has at most two levels: top-level tasks with sub-tasks directly beneath them, and nothing nested deeper.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: A monorepo package keeps its specs in its own folder rather than at the repository root, and the request says only where the spec files are. The two hard criteria are an outage rule (security still goes out, the rest is held and retried) and a validation rule that spans the service and the page. Tests that the plan lands with the spec (r12), covers both (r06), links criteria (r01) and splits the gate, queue and digest (r07).

scenarios.title: Implementation plan for appointment booking
scenarios.prompt:
Below are the approved requirements and design for appointment booking. Can you write the implementation plan for the coding agent?

Requirements

1. Availability
1.1 A provider sets weekly working hours and can block specific dates.
1.2 Slots are 30 minutes long and are shown to customers in their own time zone.

2. Booking
2.1 A customer can book an open slot. Two customers can never hold the same slot.
2.2 A slot is held for 10 minutes while the customer pays. If payment is not completed the slot opens again.
2.3 Slots less than 2 hours away cannot be booked.

3. Changes
3.1 A customer can cancel up to 24 hours before the start for a full refund. A later cancellation gets no refund.
3.2 A customer can reschedule once, up to 24 hours before the start.
3.3 A provider can cancel at any time. The customer is refunded in full and told by email.

4. Reminders
4.1 Customers get an email reminder 24 hours before and an SMS 1 hour before, unless they have opted out of SMS.
4.2 When an appointment is cancelled or rescheduled its pending reminders are cancelled.

5. Access
5.1 Providers see only their own calendar. Front-desk staff see every provider's calendar.
5.2 Customers see only their own bookings.

Design
- Provider, WorkingHours, BlockedDate, Slot and Booking items in one DynamoDB table.
- AvailabilityService: turns hours and blocked dates into slots, in UTC.
- BookingService: claims a slot with a conditional write, holds it with a TTL, and confirms it when the payment event arrives.
- PaymentClient: existing client, used for charges and refunds.
- PolicyService: applies the cancellation and reschedule windows and the 2 hour cutoff.
- ReminderScheduler: creates one-time EventBridge Scheduler entries and deletes them when an appointment changes.
- Notifier: email and SMS.
- API handlers with an AccessGuard that knows the provider, front-desk and customer roles.
- Calendar and booking pages in the web app.
rubric: A task covers reopening a held slot when payment is not completed within 10 minutes (2.2).
A task covers cancelling pending reminders when an appointment is cancelled or rescheduled (4.2).
A task covers front-desk staff seeing every provider's calendar while providers see only their own (5.1).
Every task names the numbered requirements it serves.
Availability, booking, policy and reminders each get their own tasks or sub-tasks; no single task builds the whole booking system.
Tasks build on earlier ones: the data items and the availability service come before the booking service, and the booking service comes before the API handlers and the pages.
Each task says what to create or change by name, such as the services, items or handlers from the design, and not only a goal.
Sub-tasks are shown nested beneath the parent task they belong to, not as a flat list.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: The largest feature of the set: five areas, nine design components, time-based rules and a payment hold. A plan with a few big steps ("build availability", "build booking", "build reminders") is easy to write and hard for a coding agent to carry out. The clean-up rules (hold expiry, reminder cancellation) and the role rule sit at the end of their groups.

scenarios.title: Implementation plan for a feature flag service
scenarios.prompt:
The requirements and design for the feature flag service are approved and the files are in .kiro/specs/feature-flags/. Please write the implementation plan for the coding agent.

Requirements

1. Managing flags
1.1 An admin can create a flag with a key, a description and a default value of on or off.
1.2 Keys use lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, are unique, and cannot be changed after creation.
1.3 Each flag has its own settings for dev, staging and prod.

2. Targeting
2.1 A flag can be on for a percentage of users. A given user always gets the same answer.
2.2 A flag can be on for named users and named groups. Named users override the percentage.
2.3 Raising the percentage, for example from 20 to 30, never turns the flag off for a user who already had it on.

3. Evaluating
3.1 The SDK answers from a local cache in under 5 ms.
3.2 The SDK refreshes its cache every 30 seconds. If the service is unreachable it keeps using the last values it has.
3.3 If it has no cache yet and the service is unreachable, it uses the flag's default value.

4. Safety and audit
4.1 Only admins can change prod settings. Developers can change dev and staging.
4.2 Every change records who made it and the old and new values.
4.3 A change to prod needs a reason of at least 10 characters.
4.4 Flags that nobody has evaluated for 90 days are listed as stale.

Design
- Flag, FlagEnvConfig and AuditEntry tables in Postgres.
- FlagRepository and AuditRepository.
- FlagService: create, update and list. It validates keys, checks the environment permission and writes the audit entry in the same transaction.
- Evaluator: pure function that hashes the user key and flag key into a bucket from 0 to 99 and applies the overrides and the percentage.
- Config endpoint: GET /sdk/config returns every flag for an environment, with an ETag.
- SDK: a Node package with the cache, the refresh loop and the evaluate call.
- Admin API and admin page.
- StaleReport: scheduled job that lists stale flags.
rubric: A task covers raising the percentage never turning the flag off for a user who already had it on, with a test (2.3).
A task covers requiring a reason of at least 10 characters for a change to prod (4.3).
A task covers using the flag's default value when there is no cache and the service cannot be reached (3.3).
Says the plan is saved in .kiro/specs/feature-flags/ with the requirements and design, and names no other location for it.
Every task names the numbered requirements it serves.
Tasks build on earlier ones: the repositories come before the flag service, the evaluator and the config endpoint before the SDK, and the flag service before the admin API and page.
Each task says what to create or change by name, such as the classes, functions or endpoints from the design, and not only a goal.
Requirement references appear in the same place and the same form in every task, for example always on the last line of the task.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: Fourteen criteria in which three are behaviours that live in the details: a percentage that only grows the audience, a reason required on prod changes, and a default when nothing is cached. They are easy to drop or to fold into a generic step. The folder is given as the usual spec location, so this is also a control for the location rule.
